name: Marrakech-Menara Airport
description: Marrakech-Menara Airport has two terminals housed in one complex. Both terminals have money exchange offices, and there is an ATM in the arrivals hall of Terminal 2. On ATMs, check for the Maestro, Cirrus or Plus logos to be sure that the machine accepts foreign credit cards. Some ATMs work only in French. If your card is taken at the ATM, tell airport security and they can help you get it back.…

name: Train station
description: For train schedules check out the

name: Supratours Terminal
description: Supratours buses depart from just southwest of the train station (see above).

name: Gare Voyageurs
description: CTM operates a separate bus station. You can buy the tickets in advance. The CTM's offices are better than at the Gare Routière, and there are no people trying to push you to their bus company. The office and station on Zerktouni street does not exist anymore. CTM has also an office at the long distance bus station (see above) if you just want to buy your tickets in advance or check the schedule.

name: Gare Routière
description: Most

name: Jardin Sidi Mimoun
description: Jump off point for minibuses to

name: Medina
description: The Medina is the old city quarter located within the sandstone city walls that give Marrakech the nickname the Red City. As an ancient hub, it contains a maze of narrow streets and outdoor marketplaces.

name: Djemaa El-Fna
description: The highlight of any Marrakech night. Musicians, dancers, and story tellers pack this square at the heart of the medina, filling it with a cacophony of drum beats and excited shouts. Scores of stalls sell a wide array of Moroccan fare (see the Eat section) and you will almost certainly be accosted by women wanting to give you a henna tattoo. Amateur boxing matches are sometimes held. Enjoy the va…

name: The Souks
description: Markets of Marrakech, just adjacent to Place Djemaa El-Fna, are where you can buy almost anything, from spices to shoes, jellabas to kaftans, and tea pots to tagines. Undoubtedly, being a foreigner means you will end up paying higher prices than a native would, but be sure to bargain nonetheless. If you happen to run out of dirham, you will also find plenty of people in the souks who will eagerly…

name: Koutoubia Mosque
description: Named after the booksellers market that used to be located here. It is said that the minaret of the Koutoubia mosque is to Marrakech as the Eiffel Tower is to Paris. The minaret is visible from Gueliz which is connected to the Medina by Avenue Mohammed V. At night, the mosque is beautifully lit. It was completed under the reign of the Berber Almohad Caliph Yaqub al-Mansur (1184 to 1199), and has…

name: Tanneries
description: Visiting the tanneries can be an interesting experience. Even if some people tell you the area is only for locals, it is possible to visit the Tanneries without paying a youngster. After finding a tannery, ask one of the workers if you can visit it and take pictures

name: Saadian Tombs
opening_hours: generally 09:00–17:00, although visitors should check current information before travelling
price: Foreigners: adult 100 dirham, children aged 7–13 50 dirham; Moroccan nationals and residents: adult 30 dirham, child 10 dirham
description: Saadian Tombs. The tombs were built in the 16th century as the dynastic necropolis of the Saadian dynasty. The complex includes the Chamber of the Twelve Columns, the Chamber of the Mihrab, the Chamber of the Three Niches and the garden tombs. The site was rediscovered in 1917 and subsequently restored and opened to visitors. The site is relatively compact and most visitors can see the main areas…

name: Moroccan Culinary Arts Museum
description: If you are interested in food and eating culture, you will enjoy this museum. Audiovisual information about the rich culinary culture of Marocco, its ingredients, techniques and traditions. You can also touch and smell many things. They also sport a very well equipped cooking school.

name: Majorelle Gardens
price: 170 dirham, 30 dirham extra for the Berber Museum
description: It provides an excellent respite from the hustle and bustle of the city streets, if not crowded by tourists as it sometimes is. The park was designed by the artist Jacques Majorelle in the 1920s and 1930s. Since 1980 the garden has been owned by Yves Saint-Laurent and Pierre Bergé. It boasts a collection of plants from around the globe, including what seems like every cactus species on the planet…

name: Yves Saint Laurent Museum
price: 120 dirham, combination ticket with Majorelle Gardens and Berber Museum 180 dirham, queues are far shorter here than at the gardens to buy tickets though you have to buy either a YSL Museum ticket or combination ticket
description: Advance bookings must be made online, it is not possible to buy a ticket at the site.

name: Dar Si Saïd Museum
price: Locals: adult 10 dirham, child below 12 3 dirham; tourists: adult 30 dirham
description: Museum set in an old palace with beautiful gardens. While somewhat run-down, it is worth seeing and houses many different artifacts from Morocco through the ages, such as wood carvings, musical instruments, and weapons. It is dedicated to the Moroccan craft industry of wood, gathering a very beautiful collection of popular art: carpets, clothing, pottery and ceramics. All these objects are region…

name: Ben Youssef Madrasa
description: One of the largest madrassas in North Africa. It is a school attached to the Ben Youssef Mosque and is home to beautiful art and architecture. Build ca 1570.

name: El Bahia Palace
price: Foreigners: adult 100 dirham, child aged 7–13 50 dirham; Moroccan/resident: adult 30 dirham, child aged 7–13 10 dirham
description: An ornate palace complex built in the late 19th century, with courtyards, gardens, richly decorated rooms and traditional Moroccan architectural details. The palace was developed in several stages and expanded by Ba Ahmed, Grand Vizier to Sultan Moulay Abdelaziz. The complex covers about 8 hectares. The main entrance is on Rue Riad Zitoun el Jedid. The palace is relatively close to other attracti…

name: El Badi Palace
price: Foreigners: adult 100 dirham, child aged 7–13 50 dirham; Moroccan/resident: adult 30 dirham, child aged 7–13 10 dirham
description: The palace complex is extensive, with ruins, courtyards, underground passages and exhibitions. The terrace offers views over the surrounding Medina and the Atlas Mountains on clear days. Allow around 45–90 minutes to explore the main areas. Visitors should check current information before travelling. (updated Aug 2026)

name: The Menara gardens
description: A mixture of orchards and olive groves surrounding the water reservoir with the central pavilion which is a popular sight on tourist postcards. Not a decorative garden, and now quite run down. The pavilion was built during the 16th-century Saadi dynasty, and renovated in 1869. It has a small cafe, but it is not open all hours. There are no toilets open when the cafe is closed.

name: Jewish Cemetery
description: The largest Jewish cemetery in Morocco, characterized by white-washed tombs and sandy graves. The men selling tickets are full of interesting information about the cemetery but you have to ask.

name: Slat Al Azama Synagogue
description: Synagogue which is not only a place of worship with a beautiful open courtyard, but also includes interesting displays about Judaism's varied history in Morocco, including photos of Jews in the Berber Mountains.

name: Marrakech Museum
description: It's housed in the Dar Menebhi Palace, constructed at the end of the 19th century.

name: Musée de la Palmeraie
description: In old agricultural buildings in the Palmeraie, made out of rammed earth. The architecture itself is interesting if you haven't seen it. It offers a small collection of contemporary art, with a room dedicated to Moroccan artists (also famous ones), the international ones are rather not top-notch. The gardens are nicely made and are good place to relax in quiet.

name: Musee Farid Belkahia
description: A museum dedicated to the renowned contemporary artist Farid Belkahia, showcasing different periods of his work

name: Maison de la Photographie
description: A little photography museum, it has one of the highest roof terraces in the Medina. Ticket is also valid for Museum of Mouassin Music.

name: Ali Ben Youssef Mosque
description: The first mosque in Marrakesh was erected at this place by the Almoravid emir Yusuf ibn Tashfin in the 1070s. However, it was almost completely rebuilt in early 19th century by the Alaouite sultan Suleiman, with hardly any trace left of its original Almoravid or Almohad design. Non-Muslims are not allowed to enter it.

name: Agdal Gardens
description: It consists of groves of orange, lemon, fig, apricot and pomegranate trees in rectangular plots, linked by olive-lined walkways. Together with the medina of Marrakech and the Menara Gardens, the Agdal Gardens were listed by UNESCO as a World Heritage Site in 1985.

name: Almoravid Koubba
description: A very small but intricate domed pavilion, known for being the only surviving example of Almoravid religious architecture (early 12th century) in Marrakech. Located across the street from the Ben Youssef Mosque, it is believed to have been an annex of the former Almoravid mosque. It was excavated in the 20th century after being half-buried for centuries. The pavilion's exterior can be easily seen…

name: Jbilets Geological Site
description: Explore the Berber village on a desert tour.

name: Anima garden
description: One of the prettiest gardens in the world. Created by André Heller, it is true oasis when you’re weary of the medina hubbub. Book the official shuttle bus to get there and back for free.

name: Chez Ali Fantasia
description: Horse show, acrobats on Arabian horses firing rifles in the air, horseback acrobatics, belly dancing, etc. It takes place at night in a huge imitation of an old castle.

name: Stade de Marrakesh
description: This is multi-use but mostly for football, with a capacity of 41,356. It's the home ground of Kawkab, who play in Botola 2 the second tier. In 2025 / 26 it hosted matches in the Africa Cup of Nations.

name: Marrakech Paragliding
description: Leave the city behind and discover the incredible beauty of Morocco from above! Enjoy an exciting tandem paragliding experience near Marrakech, surrounded by the spectacular Atlas Mountains.

name: Les Bains de Marrakech
address: 2 Derb Sedra, Bab Agnaou (same building as Riad Mehdi)
description: Tourists-oriented in good sense: couples can have hammam together in a private room. Extensive list of massages and spa treatments from 30 min to a full day. Reception and attendants are proficient in speaking English, however, the scrubbing and massage personnel speak only very basic vocabulary. You need to book two days in advance.

name: Thai marrakech
address: Résidence Les Jasmins Apt N° 13 4ème étage Angle Av. Mohamed v et Rue Oum Errabia Guéliz
description: Bann Thai institute is a beauty center based in the heart of Marrakech. His team is a graduate of the famous school of Wat Po in Bangkok. The center offers several Thai massage relaxation with a traditional Moroccan hammam natural products

name: Hamam Essalama
description: Friendly staff, however, no English or French (other locals helped without any problem)

name: Ô Bain de Lina
address: N 1, 84 Avenue Hassan II Residence El Faroukia
description: Friendly staff, however, no English or French; other customers likely to help you out.

name: Go Marrakech Desert Trips
description: Local tour operator offering shared and private trips between Marrakech, Merzouga and Fes. The company organizes 2–4 day Sahara tours including camel rides, overnight camps at Erg Chebbi, transportation, and optional hotel upgrades. Useful for travellers looking for clear itineraries and fixed-price desert routes.

name: Morocco Desert Guide
description: Licensed tour operator offering private and shared desert tours from Marrakech to Merzouga and Erg Chebbi. Camel trekking, overnight desert camps, and multi-day Sahara experiences. English, French and Arabic spoken.

name: Les établissements Bouchaïb
price: Check out the prices on the webpage before you go to get and idea of the cost of the items you are interested in
description: Huge two-story store with fixed prices. Carpets, spices, argon oil, jewelry, ceramics, furniture, wood handcrafts, etc.

name: Chez Monseur Michelin
description: Handmade bags and fashion items made from recycled tires and inner tubes.

name: Faissal
description: Tiny workshop making scarves in wool, cotton, and linen.

name: Maison du Caftan
description: Boutique specializing in traditional Moroccan caftans.

name: Chez Chegrouni
description: Their vegetarian couscous is supposedly the only true vegetarian couscous in town; it's also bland but they give you plenty of it. Prices go up if you sit on the terrace. Usually packed full of good-time tourists.

name: Chez Yassine
description: Not much choice but served by very friendly people. Tajines and pizzas are great and you can also order skewers that are not on the menu.

name: Henna Cafe
description: A pretty little cafe on 3 floors with an orange sign on the Berber hand-carved wooden facade opened in November 2011. You can have a cup of tea or coffee or simple lunch with dessert or just a sandwich. The Henna Café offers safe henna body adornment as well-ranging from a 50 dirham small motif on your hand to a full arm complex design for a wedding from 500 dirham. All profits go to local causes…

name: Chez Bismilah
description: Amazing food and wonderful service. The owner is very kind and the fantastic chef is a humble lady who cooks perfectly all the traditional Moroccan recipes. Tayine Royale is recommended. The roof top has an amazing view over the old medina.

name: Café Babouche medina
description: In a small street a few steps from the Jemaa El Fna square. You can eat there in a friendly atmosphere. The veal tagine with prunes and almonds is spectacular.

name: Black Pan
description: Italian restaurant. Artisanal pizzas, traditional Italian dishes and warm atmosphere.

name: Associacion Amal
opening_hours: Lunch: daily 12:00-16:00, dinner: groups of min. 10 people by reservation only
description: Here you can experience lunch similar to what Moroccans eat at home: this women's aid association provides women with education in exchange for food which is then sold for financing the model.

name: 16 Café
description: Moroccan kitchen. 16 café is caterer of events and weddings.

name: Café Arabe
description: They have a Moroccan and an Italian cook, so there are two menus to choose from. There are three floors including the downstairs courtyard which is lovely for lunch. The top floor terrace has fantastic views, you can lounge on their sofas sipping a cocktail and watching the sun go down over the medina.

name: sky mabrouka
description: Serves the same standard fare as everywhere else in a little courtyard or terrace.

name: Al Fassia
description: Traditional Moroccan food in cozy restaurant run by women (except the doorman). Wine served by the bottle.

name: Café du Livre
description: A western style bookshop-café in the villa nouvelle

name: Café Kabash
description: Have a roof terrace with a good view. Daily Moroccan menus with tea and juice.

name: Le Marrakchi
address: Place jeema el-fna, 52 Rue des Banques
description: With two main courses and wine running at around 300 dirham, this is one of the poshest restaurants in the square. The food is not necessarily better than elsewhere, but it is one of the few restaurants that serves alcohol. It also has a completely enclosed upstairs terrace, which is ideal for views of the square when the weather is bad.

name: Le Bistrot Loft
description: Steaks, bistro food and good wines. Bar with beer, aperitifs and cocktails.

name: Diaffa
description: An upscale restaurant in one of the oldest buildings in the Medina, and offers Moroccan cuisine in an ambiance that recalls the Orient at the height of its magic and glory. The food, building (whether the tables around the central courtyard and fountain or the second-level balcony), and tactful and tasteful entertainment.

name: Dar Najat's Kitchen
address: Douar Groua, derb lalla chacha, N.18
description: Daily fresh food in a boutique riad.

name: Pepe Nero
price: 400 dirham for 3-4 course dinner, wine for 200 dirham
description: Fine Italian and Moroccan dining in gorgeous Riad. Often full so make a reservation.

name: La Villa des Orangers
price: 700 dirham for three-course menu. 500 dirham for a bottle of wine.
description: French gastronomic cuisine in a very calm and pleasant atmosphere. Enjoy your dinner in soft chairs, among dark woodpanels, bookcases and artwork. In the winter start with a drink at the fireplace.

name: Le Grand Café de la Poste
address: Boulevard El mansour Eddahbi and Avenue Imam Malik
description: French brasserie with Moroccan influence in the former post office.

name: Le Grand Salon
description: Upscale restaurant with French cuisine. Serve organic vegetables and olive oil from its own gardens.

name: Dar Yacout
address: 79, derb Sidi Ahmed Soussi, Bab Doukkala
description: Traditional Moroccan gastronomic cuisine. Has a terrace overlooking the Medina.

name: Le Foundouk
description: Moroccan and European cuisine. Roof terrace and bar.

name: Les Jardins de la Medina
description: Traditional and modern Moroccan cuisine. Moroccan wine served by bottle and glass. Stylish restaurant with tall white columns.

name: Eloomm
description: Mediterranean restaurant where slow dining meets Moroccan produce.

name: Chesterfield Pub
description: A slightly unusual experience, apparently an 'English pub' it serves Moroccan lager and has an outside pool in a courtyard with palm trees, not an entirely English experience. Much less touristy than it sounds with a mainly local clientele. It serves a decent pint.

name: Le Salama
description: Happy hour from 17:00 until they close, mostly western pop classics on the top floor. Very touristy with shishas, belly dancing and waiters who wear a fez - none of it is typically Moroccan but the overall atmosphere is between relaxed and party vibe. Also offers traditional Moroccan snacks. Good for smaller (up to 10 people) groups.

name: Hotel Grand Tazi
description: The hotel has a public bar, serving beer and wine and is not overly expensive.

name: Narwama
description: Restaurant and bar that has a fire fountain in the centre and an open roof around the patio. The atmosphere is very chilled and their food is very good, but slightly expensive. Good for pre-dinner drinks.

name: Montecristo
description: Nightclub with rooftop terrace

name: Jad Mahal
description: Lounge bar and formal restaurant.

name: Sky Lounge
description: Fashionable rooftop lounge on top of the Pearl Hotel

name: Comptoir Darna
description: Cocktail bar and night club Dress code: elegant

name: African Chic
description: Moroccan Latin Brazilian. Also has a restaurant with a view to the dance floor.

name: Dar Attajmil
description: Centrally located and easy to reach, Dar Attajmil has a sand colored courtyard shaded by a tall banana tree; 4 double rooms with bathroom, 1 family suite with private courtyard, several cozy sitting areas, fireplace and library, a large terrace garden where breakfast and meals are served and a devoted team of 5 lovely persons; hammam, massages, cooking class available. Owner organic farm near Ess…

name: Dar Jaguar
address: 7-8 Derb El Mesfioui, Rahba Kedima, Medina
description: Dar Jaguar is an ancient riad that has been restored as a beautiful private guesthouse. It is situated in the heart of the old medina, neighbouring the exotic Place des Epices (spice market).

name: Riad Abaka
description: A spacious riad with seven beautifully furnished bedrooms and ensuite bathrooms.

name: Riad Amazigh
description: A former luxury riad, now a beautiful hostel. Doubles, singles, and dorms which house up to 8 people. Roof top terrace with nice views, unheated pool, restaurant and bar. Wi-Fi in communal areas, breakfast included. Open 24 hrs, can book activities and excursions.

name: Riad Basma
description: 5 double rooms with bathroom.

name: Riad Chennaoui
address: Riad Zitoune Jdid, Derb Sidi Fares N°01
description: Simple and basic riad in the Medina. The staff are friendly and happy to discuss Moroccan life and culture over a shisha in the evening. This place can be difficult to find – you may have to pay a local to take you there (10–20 dirham should do it, although they will ask for more).

name: Riad Cinnamon
description: Designed and rebuilt to a very high standard with attention to detail. Unexpected extras such as the loan of a local mobile phone and ipad. Dinners served on roof terrace with nice views, pools on patio and roof garden terrace. 5 rooms that can accommodate 3 to 4 people each, with an overall maximum of 16.

name: Riad Dar Eliane
description: Four spacious double bedrooms and bathrooms with A/C. Accommodation is on two floors of a restored 300 year old riad in an older quarter of Marrakesh. Ten minute walk to Jamaa el Fna.

name: Riad Iaazane
description: A restored riad with extensive use of traditional styling and ceramics, includes a roof terrace with views. Shower, internet with Wi-Fi access, washing, shisha (hooka), free mint tea, city map. An authentic local style breakfast included (08:30–11:30). The owners also operate a tour company that offers guided and structured tours of 1–3 days.

name: Riad LakLak
description: A riad built in the 17th century, which sleeps 12 in 2 suites and 3 bedrooms, that can be rented as a whole.

name: Riad Laksiba
description: £25-30 per person depending on season. A very popular Riad with UK visitors. Five bedrooms all with bespoke hand carved beds designed to be split to make twin bedrooms. From Bab Ksiba, an entrance into the Royal Kasbah quarter of the Medina, 1st right is Derb Kadi and Riad Laksiba is the last house in this little cul-de-sac. Ten minute walk to the Djemaa el-Fna main square.

name: Riad Lotus Perle
description: Riad Lotus Perle is in the Medina, in an old neighborhood near the lively souks and Djemaa El-Fna square, this is a wonderful riad composed of rooms and suites combining authenticity and modernity.

name: Riad Magellan
description: An elegant six-bedroom riad which offers a restful and relaxing atmosphere, in the Mouassine district. Traditional Moroccan meals are available as well as complementary Wi-Fi internet. Airport transfer service available on request.

name: Riad Melhoun
address: 99 Derb Sidi Moussa, Quartier de la Bahia, 40007 Marrakech Médina
description: Located in central Marrakech, a 3-minute walk from the El Badi and El Bahia Palaces, it features an interior courtyard with a swimming pool and a furnished rooftop terrace with views of the medina. Each room has traditional Moroccan decoration and en-suite shower. Guests also have access to a traditional living room with a fireplace and a lounge area with books. Free Wi-Fi is available in common…

name: Riad Naila
address: Marrakech Medina, Mosquée Sidi Ben Slimane
price: Riad Naila Marrakech is a private rental home. Prices range from €100-140 per day depending on the season for the entire house (sleeps 7 persons)
description: Riad Naila Marrakech is a gorgeous private rental home in the Medina of Marrakech built around a patio with a large roof terrace. It is in the Medina of Marrakech in a calm area a fifteen-minute walk away from the Djemaa El-Fna square. It has four bedrooms which sleep seven persons. Each bedroom has its own bath room. Additionally are available a fully equipped kitchen, a Moroccan lounge and a li…

name: Riad Dar Najat
address: Douar Graoua, Derb Lalla Chacha, No.18
description: Jacuzzi on the roof terrace, Wi-Fi throughout the riad, 7 ensuite shower and A/C accommodation with great gastronomy. French owner, friendly team and atmosphere.

name: Riad Papillon
price: Rooms range from £50-100 according to the season. Ask about any special offers and last minute deals
description: A riad with five beautiful rooms: Rose, Jasmine, Bougainvillea, Hibiscus and Geranium. It is located in the heart of the Dar el Basha antique district which is very safe. Cuisine is exceptional, service is warm and attentive but discrete. Papillon offers loan of local phone/iPad, IPhone charger, bathrobes. Breakfast and Wi-Fi internet are included. Very romantic and wonderful atmosphere with welc…

name: Hotel Riad Primavera
description: The only kosher hotel in all of Morocco. The kosher certification is in the lobby and is issued by the Beth Din of Marrakech. 22 rooms with personal A/C units, TVs, bathrooms with showers, decorated in typical Moroccan style. Prices tend to rise during major Jewish holidays and festivals.

name: Riad Dar Zaman
price: Rooms range from £50-100 according to the season. Askfor special offers and last minute deals.
description: A gorgeous old riad with four en suite rooms, in the historic Sidi Ben Slimane district. Cuisine is exquisite, service is warm and attentive, price includes breakfast, designer toiletries, mint tea and pastries and Wi-Fi internet. Fantastic views of Atlas Mountains from roof terrace, deliciously refreshing dipping pool, wonderful dreamy atmosphere.

name: Riad Zara
description: Run by the friendly and helpful owner Monique and her assistant Hassan. Features a rooftop terrace with nice views of Medina and cozy cane chairs, and a small pool in the center of the Riad. Traditional meals such as Tajines can be served any time of the day. Breakfast includes an array of jams, amlou, pancakes, and mint tea and can be served at flexible times. In the evening, candles are lit and…

name: Riad Zolah
description: Chic while cozy and informal riad run by Ismail and his team. The house cook, Fadila, makes fabulous fresh baked breads at breakfast. Gorgeous roof terrace and two candle-lit/petal-strewn courtyard patios (one with plunge pool).

name: Ryad Dyor
description: Riad hotel with 7 luxury suites.

name: Riad Al Loune
description: Charming Riad with pool and hammam.

name: Hotel Ali
description: Rue Moulay Ismail. Beds in en suite, dorms, and rooftop terrace mattresses for 60 dirham per person per night, including cooked breakfasts served with orange juice and fresh coffee. Dorm guests can use the internet cafe for 5 dirham per hour. They have a laundry service and free internet access for private room guests, money exchange, a terrace restaurant with views of Djemaa El-Fna, and a downst…

name: Hotel Salam (laksor)
address: bab ftouh rue haram chikh n.14, laksor, marrakech
price: 100 dirham for double room, no bathroom
description: Cheap and clean hotels, doesn't seem to have showers.

name: Hotel Atlas
description: 50 Derb Sidi Bouloukat. A 2-min walk to the famous square of Djemaa El-Fna. Clean and friendly with nice rooms with shared bathrooms. Singles from 90 dirham, doubles from 170 dirham, for 3 people 250 dirham, for 4 people 280 dirham, for 5 people 320 dirham. There are some rooms with AC for an additional 50 dirham. The hotel is charming and all arranged in the traditional way.

name: Hotel Central Palace
description: Rooms are around a noisy and echoey central courtyard. Rooms are clean, but the shared toilets can be another story. Indifferent staff and housekeepers. Nice terrace with a great view, and rooms starting at 150 dirham for a double room with shared showers and toilet. You get what you pay for, but all in all it's a good value considering that Marrakech is more expensive that most other places in M…

name: Hotel el-Ward
description: Clean, quite comfortable, and the owners are very friendly whenever they feel like it. The rooftop terrace isn't lavish, but being one of the highest it does have a great view. 60/120/170/220 dirham for single/double/triple/quadruple.

name: Hotel Essaouira
description: The hotel has singles with a shared bath from 50 dirham and doubles from 90 dirham. It is more or less like the others, but it's all painted in the traditional way, which gives it charm. Toilets and showers are bare-bones, a norm at this price range. Hot water does not stay hot for long. Overall a very good value and comfortable place from which to explore the old town.

name: Hotel Imouzzer
description: One of the cheapest and best-value hotels with rooms starting at 65 dirham for singles and 120 dirham for doubles (slightly higher in high season), all with shared bathrooms. Rooms are arranged around a traditional courtyard, and both rooms and shared bathrooms are clean with hot water. The hotel also has a comfortable terrace where you can eat breakfast for 20 dirham.

name: Hotel Sindi
description: Sud 109, Derb Sidi Bouloukat, Riad Zitoun El Kidim,

name: Hotel Smara
description: Very clean, friendly people, nice rooms. 50 dirham and doubles 80 dirham.

name: Hotel Cecil
description: At the Djemaa El-Fna, Bouloukate. Offers doorms, rooms with shared bathroom (from US$13 per person), and ensuite rooms with AC (from US$18 per person). Rooftop breakfast and Wi-Fi included.

name: Palm Plaza Hotel and Spa
address: Avenue du 7ieme Art Zone Touristique Agdal
description: . Luxurious and comfortable providing 230 rooms, including 151 twin, 52 double, 2 rooms for disabled persons, 6 junior suites, 20 senior suites and a royal suite. The hotel has a piano bar, night club and a restaurant. Snacks are available at the pool bar. The spa features a heated indoor swimming pool, a sauna, a hammam and a gym.

name: Riad Lyla
description: In Laksour district, 2 min from Djemaa El-Fna, Lyla Riad Marrakech opens its doors. Gérard is the riad's passionate owner.

name: Riad Rahba
description: Offers private, en suite rooms and is a minute from Djemaa El-Fna, at the entrance to the Souks. The Riad combines the traditional Moroccan atmosphere with the comforts of a modern hostel and hotel. The rates include breakfast and wifi. From €18 per single en suite room per night.

name: Le Vizir Center Park Resort
address: Route de Casablanca, Ouled ben Rahmoun
description: Suites decorated in 3 different styles of architecture.

name: Marrakech Rose
address: 13 Derb Laadam, Kenaria, Place Jemaa el Fna
description: Charming little hostel right in the center of town, with small dorms and super-friendly staff. Great place to meet other travellers and socialize - mostly a younger crowd. Not the best choice if you want an early night's sleep.

name: Massine II
description: 2nd backpackers in Marrakech in the old Medina. Originally a 16th century house. Central garden, and rooftop. Shower, internet, washing facilities. Breakfast is available, book early, this is a popular establishment. Some travellers complain the sheets are not changed regularly. Also, travellers aren't always registered properly.

name: The Heart of the Medina backpackers hostel
description: 1st backpackers hostel to be located in the Medina. 1 minute walk from Place Djemaa El-Fna. Rooftop terrace, hot showers, comfortable surroundings. No more than 6 beds to a room. Breakfast included as are bed linens, towels, and free Wi-Fi. You can expect to pay €8/person all year round per night if booked in advance via email or website. No lockouts, no curfews, and is open 24/7, 365 days/ year.

name: Rue Mohammed el-Hansali
description: A clean hostel with a 23:30 curfew and obligatory wake up call at 08:00. Daily daytime lockout. It is a fair distance from the action in the heart of the

name: Sirayane boutique hotel & spa
description: Spread across nearly 5 acres of gardens, this boutique hotel faces the Atlas Mountains.

name: Hotel Toulousain
